_comment: Turnkey policy attached to the bot's signing key. This file is the
source of truth — changes are PR-reviewed and applied to Turnkey via
`docs/turnkey-setup.md`.
Turnkey's policy schema continues to evolve (selector / `from` set
matching in particular). The fields below reflect the model we
design against in code; the actual JSON you upload may need shape
adjustments. Read this as 'the rules we intend to enforce', not
'the literal Turnkey JSON'.
The bot signs TWO distinct operations, so the policy is expressed as a
disjunction of two allow-branches. Each branch pins the selector, the
target-contract registry, the identity-bound actor argument, zero
value, and a rate limit. A tx must satisfy the common gates AND one
full branch.
Hard gate: every branch rule below inspects `eth.tx.*`, which is
only populated for ACTIVITY_TYPE_SIGN_TRANSACTION_V2. A future
code path (or a stamper-key compromise) that calls
ACTIVITY_TYPE_SIGN_RAW_PAYLOAD_V2 — i.e. `sign_raw_payload` for
signMessage / signTypedData — would bypass every eth.tx.* rule
because none of them reference the raw-hash surface. Pin the
policy to signTransaction so any future raw-payload signing
requires an explicit, PR-reviewed policy expansion.
Defence in depth: the tx `from` (set by Turnkey to the signing
key's own address) is automatically this key, but we re-state it
here so a future change that splits signing across multiple keys
doesn't bypass it. Applies to both branches.
Both mintFrom and submitCompletion are non-payable; reject any tx
that attaches ETH to avoid funding bugs from draining the gas
balance.
Per-operation rate limit (NOT shared with submitCompletion): capping
the two features on one counter lets a /thx burst throttle /quest
submit and vice-versa. Each branch carries its own budget so the
coupling can't happen. Turnkey's rate-limit primitive may be named
differently or live outside policy — adjust when applying. Intent:
bound mintFrom rate per signer per minute to limit blast radius of a
stamper-key compromise. Ideally keyed on selector so the two counters
are truly independent.
Only allow txs whose `to` is a Toban-registered ThanksToken
contract. The registry is a Turnkey tag set kept in sync out of
band (see `_notes`).
Function selector for the ThanksToken mint primitive (#506):
mintFrom(address,address,uint256,(uint256,address)[],bytes)
If the contract's `mintFrom` signature ever changes (including
the `RelatedRole` struct shape), recompute and update both this
selector and the matching ABI in `src/chain.ts`.
The decoded `from` argument of mintFrom (the token holder whose
allowance is being spent) must be a wallet known to the subgraph
as IdentityBound (Turnkey tag set updated by the sync cron).
Per-operation rate limit, independent of mintFrom's (see
mintFrom-rate-limit). Keeps a /quest submit burst from consuming the
/thx budget.
Only allow txs whose `to` is a Toban-registered HatsQuestModule
clone. Each workspace deploys its own quest module; the tag set
'toban-quest-module-registry' enumerates the ones the bot may
submit to (kept in sync by the same subgraph cron).
Function selector for the quest proxy primitive (#531):
submitCompletion(address,uint256,uint256)
= keccak256(sig)[0:4] = 0x947ec45f.
If the signature ever changes, recompute and update both this
selector and the matching ABI in `src/chain.ts`.
The decoded `submitter` argument (args[0]) is the member the bot
submits on behalf of. It must be an identity-bound wallet so the
bot can never attribute a submission to an arbitrary address —
same tag set the frontend/identity cron maintains.

_notes: kept in sync by an out-of-band worker / cron that reads the Toban
subgraph and calls Turnkey's tag-update API. Until that cron exists,
we operate with an explicit allowlist per set.
Both are bound to the matching ABI fragments in `src/chain.ts`.
